The type of tibial component can indeed affect mechanical alignment in unicompartmental knee replacement (UKR). Specifically, patients who received a metal-backed Onlay tibial component generally obtained better postoperative mechanical alignment compared to those who received all-polyethylene Inlay prostheses.

This is because the thicker overall construct of Onlay prostheses appears to be an important determinant of postoperative alignment. However, it's essential to note that this conclusion may not hold true for other types of tibial components or surgical approaches.

To summarize:

* Metal-backed Onlay tibial components tend to achieve better mechanical alignment.
* All-polyethylene Inlay prostheses may result in poorer postoperative alignment compared to Onlay components.

It's crucial to consider the nuances and individual variations when making surgical decisions. A healthcare professional would need to evaluate each patient's specific needs, medical history, and surgical approach to determine the best course of treatment for unicompartmental knee replacement.
